source_book: Sri Chaitanya — IPE STUDY MATERIAL for Jr. Students, Chemistry (2026-27 edition)
note: Question index for diffing and authoring; stems restated in our own wording, no solution content from the source book appears here, by policy. Numbering runs 1–41 across VSAQ and SAQ: VSAQ 27 entries (Q1–27, no sub-parts), SAQ 18 entries over 14 printed numbers (Q28–41; Q32 four parts a–d, Q34 two parts i/ii), LAQ 0 (the chapter prints no LONG ANSWER section). Then a NUMERICALS block with its OWN numbering 1–10 (15 entries: Q1 four parts a–d, Q2 three parts a–c) — indexed under section PROBLEM with refs num<n> so they do not collide with the INTEXT SOLVED PROBLEMS 6.1–6.25 (28 entries over 25 numbers; 6.12 four parts a–d), refs prob<n>. 88 entries in all. Scan page 82 is NOT nearly blank: it is printed page 84 carrying 6.22–6.25 and the chapter's closing '***'; the next chapter starts on scan page 83. Scan is clean and fully legible; the left edge of scan pages 71/73/75/77/79 is slightly curved but every number and datum was readable.

questions.stem: What does it mean to say that a reaction has reached equilibrium?
Is it correct to say that a reaction has stopped once it has reached equilibrium?
State the law of chemical equilibrium.
What is a homogeneous equilibrium? Write two homogeneous equilibrium reactions.
What is a heterogeneous equilibrium? Write two heterogeneous equilibrium reactions.
Define equilibrium constant.
Write the relation between Kp and Kc.
Under what condition are Kp and Kc numerically equal for a reaction?
Give two chemical equilibrium reactions for which Kp = Kc.
On what factors does the value of the equilibrium constant depend?
questions.notes: Printed as 'value of equation constant' — typo for 'equilibrium constant'.

questions.stem: Does changing the concentrations of the reactants change the numerical value of the equilibrium constant?
What is the effect of pressure on a gaseous chemical equilibrium?
What is the effect of increasing the concentration of the reactants on a chemical reaction that is at equilibrium?
Can a catalyst disturb the state of equilibrium?
Write any two factors that affect the equilibrium constant.
questions.notes: Printed as 'factors effecting equilibrium constant' — typo for 'affecting'.

questions.stem: Give two applications of the equilibrium constant.
What is a Bronsted base? Give one example.
What is a Bronsted acid? Give one example.
What is a Lewis acid? Give one example.
What is a Lewis base? Give one example.
What is meant by the ionic product of water?
What is the value of Kw at room temperature? What are its units?
Give two examples of salts whose aqueous solutions are basic.
Give two examples of salts whose aqueous solutions are acidic.
questions.notes: Printed as 'whose aqueous solutions are acids' — typo for 'acidic'.

questions.stem: Why are the solutions of salts formed from a strong acid and a strong base neutral?
Which equation is used to calculate the pH of an acidic buffer?
In an industrial process such as the Haber process for ammonia synthesis, how does removing a product shift the equilibrium?
Derive the relation between Kp and Kc for an equilibrium reaction.
Define equilibrium constant. Write the equilibrium constant expression for the reaction H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g) and for its reverse reaction. How are the two equilibrium constants related?
Explain the Arrhenius concept of acids and bases. What are its limitations?
What is a conjugate acid-base pair? Illustrate with examples.
Write the conjugate acid and the conjugate base of OH⁻.
questions.notes: Four-part question: (a) OH⁻ (b) H₂O (c) HCO₃⁻ (d) H₂O₂.

questions.stem: Write the conjugate acid and the conjugate base of H₂O.
Write the conjugate acid and the conjugate base of HCO₃⁻.
Write the conjugate acid and the conjugate base of H₂O₂.
What is the common ion effect? Illustrate it.
Define solubility product. Write the solubility product expression for A₂X₃.
questions.notes: The definition 'Define solubility product' is the common lead-in printed once before the two parts (i) A₂X₃ and (ii) Zr₃(PO₄)₄; it is repeated in each part's stem here.

questions.stem: Define solubility product. Write the solubility product expression for Zr₃(PO₄)₄.
Explain the term "hydrolysis of salts" with examples.
Write a short note on buffer solutions.
The aqueous solution of NH₄Cl is acidic. Explain why.
The aqueous solution of CH₃COONa is basic. Explain why.
What is Le Chatelier's principle? Discuss briefly the factors that can influence an equilibrium.
questions.notes: Printed as 'Lechatelier's principle' (one word) here and in Q40/Q41.

questions.stem: Discuss the application of Le Chatelier's principle to the industrial synthesis of ammonia (the Haber process).
Discuss the application of Le Chatelier's principle to the industrial synthesis of sulphur trioxide.
Calculate the pH of 10⁻³ M HCl.
questions.notes: Printed label NUMERICALS 1 (a). The NUMERICALS block restarts numbering at 1 after SAQ 41 and precedes the INTEXT SOLVED PROBLEMS; indexed under PROBLEM with num<n> refs. The book prints 'P^H' (capital P, superscript H) for pH throughout this block. Four parts: (a) 10⁻³ M HCl (b) 10⁻³ M H₂SO₄ (c) 10⁻⁶ M HNO₃ (d) 0.05 M H₂SO₄.

questions.stem: Calculate the pH of 10⁻³ M H₂SO₄.
Calculate the pH of 10⁻⁶ M HNO₃.
Calculate the pH of 0.05 M H₂SO₄.
Calculate the pH of 0.001 M NaOH.
questions.notes: Printed label NUMERICALS 2 (a). Three parts: (a) 0.001 M NaOH (b) 0.01 M Ca(OH)₂ (c) 0.01 M NaOH.

questions.stem: Calculate the pH of 0.01 M Ca(OH)₂.
Calculate the pH of 0.01 M NaOH.
questions.notes: Printed label NUMERICALS 2 (c). Printed as '0.01 NaOH' with the unit M omitted; the working treats it as 0.01 M.

questions.stem: A 0.005 M H₂SO₄ solution is diluted 100 times. Calculate the pH of the diluted solution.
50 ml of 0.1 M NH₄OH and 25 ml of 2 M NH₄Cl are used to make a buffer. What is its pH if pKa is 4.8?
questions.notes: Printed label NUMERICALS 4. AMBIGUOUS DATUM: the stem says 'pKa is 4.8', but NH₄OH/NH₄Cl is a basic buffer whose Henderson form needs the pKb of NH₄OH; the book's own working uses 4.8 as pKb. Probable typo for pKb.

questions.stem: A buffer is prepared by mixing 50 ml of 0.2 M CH₃COOH and 25 ml of 0.4 M CH₃COONa. If pKa is 4.8, what is the pH of the solution?
questions.notes: Printed label NUMERICALS 5. The stem starts at the foot of printed page 78; its working is on page 79.

questions.stem: One litre of a buffer solution contains 0.1 mole of acetic acid and 1 mole of sodium acetate. Find its pH if the pKa of CH₃COOH is 4.8.
questions.notes: Printed label NUMERICALS 6. Printed as '0.1 mole of acetic acid add 1 mole of sodium acetate' — 'add' is a typo for 'and'.

questions.stem: Calculate the pH of one litre of a buffer solution containing 1 M formic acid (HCOOH) and 0.1 M sodium formate (HCOONa), given that the pKa of formic acid is 3.75.
questions.notes: Printed label NUMERICALS 7. Printed wording repeats itself ('Calculate the pH ... Find its pH.') and spells 'solition'; one question.

questions.stem: The solubility of Ag₂CrO₄ is 1.3 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹. What is its solubility product?
The solubility of A₂B is 2 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹. What is its solubility product?
The solubility product of a salt AB is 10⁻¹⁰ mol² L⁻². What is its solubility?

For the formation of NH₃ from N₂ and H₂, the following equilibrium concentrations were obtained at 500 K: [N₂] = 1.5 × 10⁻² M, [H₂] = 3.0 × 10⁻² M and [NH₃] = 1.2 × 10⁻² M. Calculate the equilibrium constant.
questions.notes: Printed label 6.1 (INTEXT SOLVED PROBLEMS; the block mirrors NCERT Class-11 Chapter 7 worked examples 7.1–7.25).

questions.stem: In a sealed vessel at 800 K the equilibrium concentrations are N₂ = 3.0 × 10⁻³ M, O₂ = 4.2 × 10⁻³ M and NO = 2.8 × 10⁻³ M. What is Kc for the reaction N₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2NO(g)?
PCl₅, PCl₃ and Cl₂ are at equilibrium at 500 K with concentrations 1.59 M PCl₃, 1.59 M Cl₂ and 1.41 M PCl₅. Calculate Kc for the reaction PCl₅ ⇌ PCl₃ + Cl₂.
For the equilibrium 2NOCl(g) ⇌ 2NO(g) + Cl₂(g), the value of the equilibrium constant Kc is 3.75 × 10⁻¹ at 1069 K. Calculate Kp for the reaction at this temperature.
questions.notes: Printed label 6.4. PROBABLE PRINTED TYPO: the stem gives Kc = 3.75 × 10⁻¹, but the book's own working and the NCERT source (Example 7.4) use Kc = 3.75 × 10⁻⁶. Kept as printed.

questions.stem: The value of Kc for the reaction 2A ⇌ B + C is 2 × 10⁻³. At a given time the composition of the reaction mixture is [A] = [B] = [C] = 3 × 10⁻⁴ M. In which direction will the reaction proceed?

13.8 g of N₂O₄ was placed in a 1 L reaction vessel at 400 K and allowed to reach the equilibrium N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g). The total pressure at equilibrium was found to be 9.15 bar. Calculate Kc, Kp and the partial pressures at equilibrium.
The value of ΔG⊖ for the phosphorylation of glucose in glycolysis is 13.8 kJ/mol. Find the value of Kc at 298 K.
The hydrolysis of sucrose, Sucrose + H₂O ⇌ Glucose + Fructose, has equilibrium constant Kc = 2 × 10¹³ at 300 K. Calculate ΔG⊖ at 300 K.
What are the conjugate bases of the following Bronsted acids: HF, H₂SO₄ and HCO₃⁻?
questions.notes: Printed label 6.9. The stem is on printed page 80; its answer is on page 81.

questions.stem: Write the conjugate acids of the following Bronsted bases: NH₂⁻, NH₃ and HCOO⁻.
The species H₂O, HCO₃⁻, HSO₄⁻ and NH₃ can act both as Bronsted acids and as Bronsted bases. For each species give the corresponding conjugate acid and conjugate base.
Classify HO⁻ as a Lewis acid or a Lewis base and show how it acts as such.
questions.notes: Printed label 6.12 (a). Four parts: (a) HO⁻ (b) F⁻ (c) H⁺ (d) BCl₃.

questions.stem: Classify F⁻ as a Lewis acid or a Lewis base and show how it acts as such.
Classify H⁺ as a Lewis acid or a Lewis base and show how it acts as such.
Classify BCl₃ as a Lewis acid or a Lewis base and show how it acts as such.
The concentration of hydrogen ion in a sample of a soft drink is 3.8 × 10⁻³ M. What is its pH?
Calculate the pH of a 1.0 × 10⁻⁸ M solution of HCl.

The ionisation constant of HF is 3.2 × 10⁻⁴. Calculate the degree of dissociation of HF in its 0.02 M solution. Also calculate the concentration of all the species present (H₃O⁺, F⁻ and HF) in the solution, and its pH.
The pH of a 0.1 M monobasic acid is 4.50. Calculate the concentrations of the species H⁺ and HA at equilibrium. Also determine the values of Ka and pKa of the monobasic acid.
questions.notes: Printed label 6.16. The printed stem lists only H⁺ and HA; the NCERT source (Example 7.16) asks for H⁺, A⁻ and HA. Kept as printed.

questions.stem: Calculate the pH of a 0.08 M solution of hypochlorous acid, HOCl. The ionization constant of the acid is 2.5 × 10⁻⁵. Also determine the percent dissociation of HOCl.
The pH of a 0.004 M hydrazine solution is 9.7. Calculate its ionization constant Kb and its pKb.
Calculate the pH of a solution in which 0.2 M NH₄Cl and 0.1 M NH₃ are present. The pKb of ammonia solution is 4.75.

Determine the degree of ionization and the pH of a 0.05 M ammonia solution. The ionization constant of ammonia can be taken from Table 7.7. Also calculate the ionization constant of the conjugate acid of ammonia.
questions.notes: Printed label 6.20. EXTERNAL DATUM: 'Table 7.7' is the NCERT Class-11 table of base ionization constants and is not reprinted in this book; the value it supplies is Kb(NH₃) = 1.77 × 10⁻⁵.

questions.stem: Calculate the pH of a 0.10 M ammonia solution. Then calculate the pH after 50.0 mL of this solution is treated with 25.0 mL of 0.10 M HCl. The dissociation constant of ammonia is Kb = 1.77 × 10⁻⁵.
The pKa of acetic acid and the pKb of ammonium hydroxide are 4.76 and 4.75 respectively. Calculate the pH of an ammonium acetate solution.
Calculate the solubility of A₂X₃ in pure water, assuming that neither kind of ion reacts with water. The solubility product of A₂X₃ is Ksp = 1.1 × 10⁻²³.
The Ksp values of two sparingly soluble salts, Ni(OH)₂ and AgCN, are 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁵ and 6 × 10⁻¹⁷ respectively. Which salt is more soluble? Explain.
Calculate the molar solubility of Ni(OH)₂ in 0.10 M NaOH. The ionic product of Ni(OH)₂ is 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁵.
questions.notes: Printed label 6.25. Last question of the chapter; the '***' end mark follows its answer on printed page 84.
